placement_test.prompt: A clinic is sorting four pieces of work. Which one is a project rather than operations?
options: Sending appointment reminders to patients every evening
Ordering medical supplies whenever the stock runs low
Moving all patient records onto a new booking system
Cleaning and preparing the treatment rooms each day
placement_test.explanation: A project is temporary and produces something unique. Moving the records to a new system has a defined end and a one-time result. The other three repeat with no planned end, so they are operations.
placement_test.source_quote: Building a new payroll system is a project; running payroll with that system afterwards is operations.

placement_test.prompt: Three weeks before a fixed launch date, the sponsor asks for one more report to be added. What should the project manager do first?
options: Show what the report does to time and cost, then ask the sponsor to choose
Add the report quietly and ask the team to work evenings until the launch
Refuse the request, because the scope was agreed when the project began
Shorten the testing period so that the report fits before the launch date
placement_test.explanation: The constraints are linked, so added scope has to be paid for in time, money or quality. The project manager makes that trade-off visible and lets the sponsor decide, instead of absorbing it or refusing outright.
placement_test.source_quote: A good project manager makes these trade-offs visible and asks the sponsor to choose, instead of quietly absorbing the change.

placement_test.prompt: A project has two parallel routes. Activities A then B take 6 and 8 days; activities C then D take 3 and 4 days. One activity can be shortened by two days. Which choice brings the finish date forward?
options: Shorten activity C, because it starts the shorter route
Shorten activity D, because it ends the shorter route
Shorten either C or D, because both have float to spare
Shorten activity B, because it lies on the longest route
placement_test.explanation: A then B is the longest route at 14 days, so it is the critical path and sets the finish date. C then D takes 7 days and has 7 days of float, so shortening it changes nothing.
placement_test.source_quote: When a project must finish sooner, the project manager looks at critical path activities first, because shortening other activities does not change the finish date.

placement_test.prompt: A team fears that a custom part may arrive late, so it signs a fixed-price contract under which the supplier pays the cost of any delay. Which risk response is this?
options: Avoid, because the plan was changed so that the risk cannot happen
Transfer, because another party now carries the cost of the risk
Mitigate, because the team acted early to make the risk less likely
Accept, because the team set money aside in case the risk occurs
placement_test.explanation: The part can still arrive late, so the risk is not avoided, and nothing has made it less likely. The contract shifts the financial impact to the supplier, which is a transfer.
placement_test.source_quote: To transfer a risk is to shift its financial impact to a third party, typically through insurance, a warranty, or a fixed-price contract.

placement_test.prompt: A startup is building its first mobile app and expects users' wishes to change after every release. Which way of working fits best?
options: Plan every feature in detail now and build them in one long sequence
Freeze the requirements at the start and deliver everything at the end
Work in short iterations and let feedback decide what is built next
Fix the full scope first, then estimate the time and cost to deliver it
placement_test.explanation: When requirements are expected to change, short iterations that deliver working pieces and collect feedback let the plan follow what the team learns. The other three fix the scope before anything has been learned.
placement_test.source_quote: Agile suits projects where requirements are expected to change as the team learns, such as a new consumer app whose users have not yet said what they want.
